subject: Sales → CS: LumenHealth pilot — handoff, constraints, and acceptance checklist
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Elaine Park <elaine@lumenhealth.com>, Jason Rios <jason.rios@lumenhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Sales → CS: LumenHealth pilot — handoff, constraints, and acceptance checklist

Team — handing off LumenHealth (deal LUM-2027-0421). Quick summary and asks so CS can pick up the pilot planning. Elaine and Jason are copied to keep transparency on timing: they prefer kickoff the week of Mar 7.

Synopsis:
- Pilot: 8-week pilot starting with a 2-week integration/staging window, then a 6-week evaluation.
- P0 goals: integration with their API for patient-summary enrichment, <250ms median latency for single-turn calls, pre-seeding KV cache for top-500 prefixes.
- Estimated usage (pilot): ~350k tokens/week at peak; expect steady growth if results look good.
- Data residency: US-only (must stay in us-west region).
- Egress/network: they require explicit IP allowlist and advise limited outbound egress to third-party telemetry endpoints. See attached network-egress-diagram.png.

Key docs attached: Mutual Action Plan + SOW draft (attached). I left an open SLA exception in the SOW for a short canary 14-day window at 99.5% instead of standard 99.9 — to be converted post-pilot if performance stabilizes.

Open internal asks for CS/Delivery before kickoff: 
1) Confirm primary CS owner and backup.
2) Review the egress diagram — can we meet their allowlist model (static IP blocks)?
3) Confirm model/quantization profile recommended for the pilot (cost/latency trade).
4) Draft initial 2-week staging checklist (roles + tech validation steps).

Elaine/Jason — we recommended a lightweight pilot to validate latency and quality before a larger commitment. Tessa will lead the handoff.

Thanks,
David
David Kim
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: LumenHealth_MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN.xlsx (spreadsheet), SOW-draft-v2.pdf (pdf), network-egress-diagram.png (png)

Thanks David — happy to take this. Quick answers and next steps from CS perspective: 

Owner assignment:
- Primary: Tessa Morgan (CS Lead)
- Backup: Marissa Cole (Implementation PM)
- Technical owner to coordinate with infra: Ben Carter

Immediate questions for LumenHealth (Elaine):
- Do you have a fixed set of source IPs for the allowlist or would you prefer a CIDR block we can reserve?
- Which environments will send traffic to Redwood (dev/stage/prod)? We suggest testing in stage first, prod only after acceptance.

Proposed internal plan (deliverables for staging 2-week window):
- Day 0–2: Kickoff, mutual-action-plan signoff, NDA/contract redlines agreed.
- Day 3–7: Network allowlist + cert exchange, schema mapping, sample payloads.
- Day 8–12: Baseline tests (latency, failure modes, max concurrency), KV pre-seed of top-500 prefixes.
- Day 13–14: Acceptance checklist + go/no-go for pilot start.

Model recommendation request to Research: suggest running the pilot on opt-quant-16 with prefix caching; if latency is above target at 95th percentile, fallback path to opt-int8-prod. Ben — can you confirm runtime capacity estimate for 350k tokens/week?

I'll draft the staging checklist and share a first pass by EOD Thu. Elaine — are you OK with Mar 7 kickoff if staging completes on schedule?

-Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Elaine Park <elaine@lumenhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 08:41:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Sales → CS: LumenHealth pilot — handoff, constraints, and acceptance checklist

Tessa — quick capacity and infra notes:
- 350k tokens/week peak → ~75 peak concurrent token streams (assuming average request 1.2k tokens/session over busy hour). We'll reserve a 1.5x buffer (so ~115 concurrent).
- Runtime recommendation: start on opt-quant-16 as suggested. We'll configure a canary pool with 2x capacity for the first 14 days to observe tail latencies.
- IP allowlist: we can publish static egress IPs from our dedicated pool (requires a small Dedicated reservation for the pilot window). If procurement can't allocate Dedicated, we can use hosted with VPC egress overlay — requires SSO/KMS coordination.

Action items I will take:
- Create a capacity reservation request (internal ticket) and estimate monthly $ impact for the pilot.
- Draft runtime config (batching window, KV cache TTLs) and share to the staging checklist doc.

Marissa — once Tessa shares the staging checklist, I'll attach the runtime config section.

-Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks all — confirming we remain aligned. A few clarifications from our side: 
1) IP allowlist: we can provide a /28 of static egress IPs (will share in a separate secure message).
2) Environments: we will stand up a staging environment first (no PHI), then a prod environment for limited subset of non-sensitive data for acceptance. Full-PHI flow not part of pilot.
3) Security questionnaire: we started the security form with our InfoSec team. Expect to send the completed copy by Thu. Please note: we require audit logs for admin actions during the pilot window.

Mar 7 kickoff is OK as long as the staging checklist and allowlist exchange happen the week prior. We're flexible with the 14-day canary at 99.5% — as long as we receive daily latency reports and incident escalation contacts.

Elaine Park
Director, Digital Operations — LumenHealth
